messages:
cora: heads-up folks  onboarding queue backlog spiking. we're running full deep-bench for every model by default and it's chewing GPU cycles. can we agree a lighter admit gate? :grimacing:

devin: absolutely. proposal: tiered admit. 1) smoke-run (sanity + tokenizer + shape checks), 2) sampled perf/quality (short/mid/long mix), 3) trigger deep-bench only on failures or flagged diffs. keeps safety but cuts cost.

niko: +1. need to prove statistical fidelity of the sampled perf. we should capture a small set of high-leverage long examples separately (rare edge cases).

maya: operational constraints: sampling and smoke must be deterministic and reproducible (bench_v + seed). otherwise we get flaky admits and blame games. bench_v needs changelog + review process.

cora: agree on determinism. also want explicit signal taxonomy: `smoke_pass` (bool), `sampled_quality_delta` (pct), `compat_errors` (count), `p95_latency_change` (ms). infra will own emission, ML owns thresholds.

devin: tradeoff: pre-admit deep-bench increases time-to-admit for large models. for teams that want faster iteration we can offer opt-in 'fast-admit' which skips deep-bench but requires canary traffic and retention of rollback hooks.
niko: can we formalize canary policy? e.g., `fast-admit` requires: gradual ramp to 1% -> 10% -> 100% over X hours and auto-rollback on `eval_regression` or `error_rate>0.5%`.

maya: sample policy suggestion (start simple):
```
sample_policy:
  - cohort: short
    pct: 60
    max_len: 64
  - cohort: mid
    pct: 30
    max_len: 512
  - cohort: long
    pct: 10
    max_len: 2048
```

cora: love that. infra note: we'll need an efficient sampler that respects tokenizer and sequence bucketing to avoid O(N) tokenization cost per candidate. maybe reuse cached tokenization from previous runs.

devin: question about gating semantics: are we going to block admit on `compat_errors>0`? sometimes false positives happen. propose `compat_errors` >=1 raises a high-priority reviewer alert but does not auto-block unless `smoke_pass=false`.
niko: sounds reasonable. make `compat_errors` actionable: include stack traces + sample input in alert so reviewer can triage quickly.

infra-bot: created ticket #ML-7123 'tiered-admit-sampling-and-canary-policy' assigned to @devin, due 2024-07-02

maya: operational checklist items: 1) bench_v tagging and changelog 2) deterministic seeds + tokenization cache 3) sampling config in model manifest 4) dashboards for sample cohort diffs 5) canary rollback hooks + runbook.

cora: ok owners: infra implements sampler + metrics emission (@niko), ML defines thresholds + golden examples (@devin), product owns canary UX + dashboard filters (@maya). i'll put this in the RFC follow-up and reference #ML-7123.

devin: one last nit: add a small budget estimator to onboarding UI so teams know expected deep-bench cost before submit. saves surprise bills. :money_with_wings:

maya: agreed. also add `bench_v` dropdown in console so you can compare current run to historical. tiny UX win but huge for triage.

cora: thanks everyone. follow-up doc + owners incoming. if nobody objects i'll land this plan by end of week. :thumbsup:
